sections.h2: Which Colorado court handles a residential eviction?
sections.html:
Evictions are filed in the state court system, which the Colorado Judicial Branch runs through its self-help pages. According to Wikipedia, Colorado is divided into 23 judicial districts, and each has a district court and a county court with limited jurisdiction. The notices and filings described on this page lead to a case in the county where the rental house sits.

The Judicial Branch's Residential Evictions page groups its material into guides, step-by-step forms, subpoenas, frequently asked questions and more resources. It says the branch has compiled all the forms required for house, apartment or condo evictions in one place. It also points to File Without Payment for people who cannot afford the fee and to the Court Resource Centers.

Colorado has 64 counties, so the clerk you deal with depends on the property's address. A landlord with a house in one county and a home in another may have two cases in two courts.

sections.h2: What can happen if a landlord skips the proper steps?
sections.html:
A landlord who skips the legal process can be sued by the tenant. The Judicial Branch's Unlawful Evictions page says landlords must follow the right process, and if they do not, the tenant can file a lawsuit.

If the tenant wins, two remedies are listed:

  • The court can award the tenant money, called damages.
  • A district court can stop the unlawful eviction while the case is pending, which is called an injunction.

This is the main reason owners who plan to sell a rented house should not change locks, shut off utilities or remove belongings. A sale does not give the owner a shortcut around the court process.

sections.h2: How does the tenant's lawsuit move through the court?
sections.html:
The unlawful eviction forms follow a five step order. The same page lists the filings in sequence, and the answer deadline depends on the court.

StepWhat happensForms or timing listed
1Tenant starts the caseComplaint, JDF 601 cover sheet for district court, Form 1 summons for county court or JDF 600 for district court
2Tenant serves the landlordJDF 98 Affidavit of Service
3Landlord respondsDue within 14 days in county court, 21 days in district court
4Hearing preparationJDF 71 witness list, JDF 72 exhibit list, subpoena forms
5As neededJDF 205 motion to waive the filing fee; restraining order motion in district court

The restraining order motion has no standard form and is part of the district court process only.

sections.h2: Why does the notice type matter before a sale?
sections.html:
The notice you serve sets the clock for everything after it. This page's sections above describe the notice types Colorado uses and how many days each requires. Pick the one that matches the reason you are ending the tenancy, because a wrong or late notice means starting over.

An owner who wants to sell has a few paths:

  • Serve the notice that fits the situation, then sell after the tenant leaves.
  • Sell the house with the tenant still in it, to a buyer who agrees to take it that way.
  • Agree on a move-out date with the tenant in writing.
  • Sell for cash as-is and let the buyer handle the occupancy question.

Each path has a cost in time, and a buyer who needs a vacant house has to wait for the tenant to leave. A buyer who accepts an occupied house does not.

sections.h2: Do rented Colorado houses pay income tax when sold?
sections.html:
A rental house that was never your residence does not qualify for the home sale exclusion. IRS Topic 701 grants up to $250,000 of exclusion, or $500,000 on a joint return, only for a main home that passes the ownership and use tests, which each require 24 months in the five years before the sale.

Colorado follows the federal figure. The Department of Revenue's nonresident guidance says income from real property located in Colorado, including capital gains, is Colorado source income. An out of state landlord who sells a Colorado rental will usually see the closing agent withhold the lesser of 2 percent of the sale price or the net proceeds, claimable on a Colorado return.

If you ever lived in the house, the exclusion may still apply in part. Ask a tax professional before you decide.

sections.h2: What does Colorado weather and geography mean for a rented house?
sections.html:
A rented house takes the same weather as any other. Wikipedia notes that the eastern Plains are subject to some of the biggest hail storms in North America, and that severe hail hit Denver on July 11, 1990 and May 8, 2017. It also lists large wildfires, including the Marshall Fire of December 30, 2021, described as the most destructive in the state by property loss.

If a tenant dispute turns on repairs, keep photos, invoices and insurance claims in one folder.

  • Roof and gutter condition after hail seasons.
  • Defensible space around the house in wildfire areas.
  • Records of what the tenant reported and when.

sections.h2: How do Colorado regions change an eviction and sale?
sections.html:
Where the house sits changes who your buyers are and how quickly they appear. Wikipedia describes Colorado as a state of 6,012,561 people in 2025, with Denver as the capital and largest city and El Paso as the largest county. The Front Range Urban Corridor holds the main metro areas, including Denver, Colorado Springs, Pueblo and Greeley. On the Western Slope, the larger population centers are Grand Junction, Durango and Montrose.

Roughly half the state is flat and rolling land east of the Rockies, with precipitation of 15 to 25 inches a year. The rest is mountain and desert country. A rented house in a Front Range suburb and one in a small mountain town may share the same notice rules but face very different buyer pools.

sections.h2: What reporting do you owe after selling a rental house?
sections.html:
Expect paperwork even when the gain is small. Under IRS Topic 701, if you receive a Form 1099-S, you must report the sale even when the gain is excludable, and you must report it when you cannot exclude all of the gain. The IRS points to Schedule D and Form 8949 for reporting.

Colorado adds its own return. According to the Department of Revenue, nonresidents with Colorado source income must file a Colorado return when they must file a federal return or owe Colorado tax. Withholding at closing is claimed on the line for form DR 1079, not the W-2 or 1099 line, and a refund is allowed if it exceeds the tax owed.

sections.h2: What do landlords selling a house in Colorado usually run into?
sections.html:
The common problems are a tenant who stops paying, a lease that runs past the planned sale date and a house that needs work. Each one slows a standard listing, because lenders and buyers want vacant, move-in ready homes.

A cash sale as-is removes several of those steps. We buy houses in Colorado in their current condition, including rentals with tenants, and we can talk through the notice timeline before you commit. This page is general information and not legal advice, so confirm forms and deadlines with the court or a licensed attorney.

faqs.q: Can a Colorado tenant sue a landlord for an unlawful eviction?
faqs.a: Yes. The Colorado Judicial Branch says that if a landlord does not follow the right process, the tenant can file a lawsuit and may be awarded damages.

faqs.q: How long does a landlord have to answer a tenant's unlawful eviction case?
faqs.a: The response is due within 14 days in county court and within 21 days in district court, according to the Judicial Branch's forms page.

faqs.q: Where do I find Colorado eviction forms?
faqs.a: The Colorado Judicial Branch has compiled the forms for house, apartment and condo evictions on its Residential Evictions self-help page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house with a tenant in it in Colorado?
faqs.a: Yes, you can sell it, but the tenancy continues until it is lawfully ended. A buyer who will take it occupied, or a cash buyer, is usually the fastest route.

faqs.q: Is the gain on a rental house sale taxable in Colorado?
faqs.a: It can be. A house you never lived in does not meet the federal use test, and Colorado treats gain from Colorado real property as Colorado source income.
